findings.title: English source path derivation is fragile and can resolve to the wrong file or throw
findings.body: The English file path is computed with replaceAll on the absolute path: 'resources-community' -> 'resources' and a regex '_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties' -> '_en.properties'. Any directory containing an underscore or dash-letters before '.properties' in the absolute path (e.g. a checkout path like /home/u/my_repo/...) is rewritten by the second regex only at the final '.properties' occurrence, which is fine, but the first replaceAll also rewrites any path segment containing 'resources-community' anywhere, and for the admin/email files whose names have no locale suffix the regex can eat part of the base name. When the derived file does not exist, the code throws a RuntimeException rather than a MojoExecutionException, aborting the whole verification run for every module instead of reporting the problem.

findings.title: Checked IOException from file reading is turned into unchecked RuntimeException
findings.body: verifySafeHtml() reads the target and English bundles and wraps IOException in RuntimeException, while verify() is declared to throw MojoExecutionException for read failures. A missing or unreadable file therefore escapes as an unchecked exception that the Maven plugin does not handle gracefully, changing the error contract of verify().

findings.title: Sanitizer output unescaped with unescapeHtml4 can mask real illegal HTML
findings.body: The sanitized output is passed through StringEscapeUtils.unescapeHtml4 before comparison, and the input value was also unescaped in normalizeValue. Because both sides are unescaped, an input containing an escaped tag such as <script> is decoded to <script> on the input side and then compared against sanitizer output that would have stripped it; the comparison is no longer a faithful check that the raw translation contains only allowed markup, so some illegal HTML in translations may pass verification silently.

findings.title: Anchor validation compares only in lockstep and skips extra or missing anchors
findings.body: santizeAnchors iterates target anchors and advances the English matcher only when it finds one; when englishMatcher.find() fails or the tag differs it records a message and breaks, but if the target has fewer anchors than the English source, extra English anchors are never reported. Also replaceFirst with Pattern.quote removes the first occurrence in the value which may not be the matched position, so the stripped string can be wrong when the same tag appears more than once.

findings.title: Policy fields are non-private mutable instance fields and pattern fields are package-visible
findings.body: POLICY_SOME_HTML, POLICY_NO_HTML and HTML_TAGS are declared without modifiers and are recreated per instance, though they are constant. The PolicyFactory construction per file is also wasteful; these should be private static final.

findings.title: Tests use fixtures whose English counterparts are not present, so results depend on the path rewrite
findings.body: The tests for illegalHtmlTag_en.properties, noHtml_de.properties and changedAnchor_de.properties rely on the English path derived from the fixture location (e.g. noHtml_de -> noHtml_en). Fixtures like duplicateKeys_en and illegalHtmlTag_en map to themselves, so the illegal-HTML test for illegalHtmlTag_en actually compares the file against itself and only passes because of the unterminated '<div>' tag; the tests do not isolate the behaviour they claim to verify, and no test covers a valid HTML translation passing.

findings.title: Translation replaced with English-language/unrelated text and HTML links removed
findings.body: totpStep1 was changed from a localized instruction naming FreeOTP/Google Authenticator with links to a shortened sentence. The new value is still a Finnish sentence, but the links the translation previously provided (FreeOTP, Google Play) are dropped, so users lose the download guidance. Several sibling PR changes (e.g. messages_lt in account and login) replace the Lithuanian translation with Italian text ('Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:'), which is a wrong-language string shipped to Lithuanian users.

findings.title: Lithuanian account message replaced by Italian text
findings.body: totpStep1 now reads 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:' which is Italian, not Lithuanian. The same wrong-language string is introduced in login/messages_lt.properties, so Lithuanian users will see an Italian instruction.

findings.title: Chinese string uses Traditional Chinese text and a different locale from the file
findings.body: totpStep1 is set to '在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：' which mixes Traditional characters (手機, 應用程式) into the Simplified Chinese file; it should be Simplified (手机, 应用程序).

findings.title: Hungarian HTML email key corrupted by a stray '***' prefix
findings.body: The emailUpdateConfirmationBodyHtml line was changed to start with '***emailUpdateConfirmationBodyHtml=' in the diff, which would be an invalid/unknown property key (the key becomes '***emailUpdateConfirmationBodyHtml') so the real key is no longer translated and falls back to the English default, and the literal '***' is left in a properties file.

findings.title: Anchor href quoting changed in Lithuanian email HTML, adding links to a literal LT string
findings.body: The original href=LT"{0}" was corrected to href="{0}" in the HTML bodies, which is a fix, but the change also affects emailVerificationBodyHtml etc. Meanwhile the properties remain with malformed markup elsewhere; ensure the translated email HTML templates still match the anchors expected by the verifier.

findings.title: Dutch HTML body fix made outside the stated issue, still altering content
findings.body:
The emailVerificationBodyHtml change fixes an unclosed

but the new string also includes an escaped quote change; these unrelated edits widen the diff beyond the sanitizer fix and risk unintentional translation changes.

findings.title: Trailing key-value corrected but the multivalued-size choice pattern is wrong for some values
findings.body: The corrected error-invalid-multivalued-size uses {2,choice,...} for the upper bound and {1,choice,...} for the lower bound; the choice forms in this file (0#hodnôt|1#hodnotu|1<hodnoty|4<hodnôt) do not cover the 2-4 plural case correctly for values between 2 and 4 in the second branch, producing incorrect grammatical forms.

findings.title: Choice format in multivalued-size message is copied into the English key and changes rendering for admin consumers
findings.body: error-invalid-multivalued-size is changed to use a {2,choice,...} subformat, but this key is consumed via MessageFormat without the same argument typing for all callers; the English string in the admin theme and login theme now both depend on the choice syntax, and the generic change to '{{0}}'-style placeholders to '{0}' in the js/admin messages also changes how the JS i18n layer interpolates the value.
